abstract: Using data from the China Household Finance Survey (CHFS) spanning 2015 to 2019, this article examines how economic policy uncertainty (EPU) affects household allocation of risky financial assets in China. The results show that higher EPU significantly reduces the likelihood that households participate in risky financial markets, decreases both the scale and depth of risky asset holdings, and lowers allocation efficiency. Heterogeneity analyses indicate these negative effects are stronger among urban households, risk-tolerant households, and households located in second-tier areas. Mechanism analyses further reveal that EPU operates through multiple channels. Social capital mediates the relationship between EPU and risky asset allocation decisions, allocation scale, and allocation depth, but does not mediate allocation efficiency. Financial literacy mediates the effects on decisions, scale, and efficiency, but not depth. Financial information attention mediates all four dimensions. These findings offer new insights into how EPU impacts household asset allocation decisions and provide empirical evidence to inform more effective household financial policies.

title: Economic policy uncertainty and household allocation to risky financial assets in China
